summary: Turn a research goal and a segment into an interview guide: what to ask, what each question is testing, and the biases to avoid.

research_goal.title: Research goal
research_goal.description: What you need to learn, and what decision it feeds. "Whether to build X" is a decision; "how teams currently do Y" is a goal.

segment.title: Who you will talk to
segment.description: The people you can actually reach: role, context, and how they differ from the people you cannot reach.

assumptions.title: Assumptions to test
assumptions.description: What you currently believe and would be expensive to be wrong about. One per line.

framing.description: The goal restated as what this guide can and cannot establish, so the reader knows the limits before the first interview.

purpose.description: What this section is for; skip it if you are short on time and this is not load-bearing.

ask.description: The question in the words you would actually say.

testing.description: The assumption or unknown this question is aimed at.

follow_up.description: The probe to use when the first answer is generic.

listen_for.description: The specific signal in an answer that would change your mind.

question.description: A tempting question that would produce misleading data.

why.description: The bias it introduces — leading, hypothetical, or self-report where behaviour is needed.

sampling_risk.description: Who this segment excludes, and which conclusions would be unsafe as a result.
